en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

es.L: Vino a mí la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, diciendo:
es.B: La palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a mí:
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dio este mensaje:

fr.L: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée, disant :
fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée :
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a donné ce message :

sw.L: Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likanijia, kusema:
sw.B: Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likanijia:
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alinipa ujumbe huu:

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came: God gave the prophet a message
decisions.reason: This is the formula by which Jeremiah introduces a message he has received from God (1:4, 11, 13). Chapter 2 begins the first collection of his oracles, spoken to Jerusalem and Judah, with Jeremiah speaking as "me".

decisions.choice: saying: God's words follow without quotation
decisions.reason: The words after "saying" are God's own, spoken to Jeremiah and then through him to the people. As in the rest of the prophet's poetry, God's speech is not set off as a quotation; only words that the oracle puts in the people's mouths are.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: / The word of the LORD came to me: / The LORD gave me this message:
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula in Jeremiah. Balanced leaves "saying" to the colon; Readable says it plainly.

source.text: הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ בְאָזְנֵ֨ייְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה זָכַ֤רְתִּי לָךְ֙ חֶ֣סֶד נְעוּרַ֔יִךְ אַהֲבַ֖ת כְּלוּלֹתָ֑יִךְ לֶכְתֵּ֤ךְ אַחֲרַי֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בְּאֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֥א זְרוּעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Go and proclaim in [the] ears of Jerusalem, saying, Thus says Yahweh: I remember for you [the] loyal love of your youth, [the] love of your betrothals, your walking after me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.

en.L: Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem, saying, Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q I remember for you the loyal love of your youth, \q the love of your bridal days, \q your walking after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the wilderness, \q in a land not sown.
en.B: Go and call out so that Jerusalem hears: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q I remember the loyal love of your youth, \q how you loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as a bride, \q how you went after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through the wilderness, \q through a land where nothing was sown.
en.R: Go and announce this to the people of Jerusalem. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q I remember the faithful love you showed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when you were young. \q You loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like a bride. \q You followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through the desert, \q through a land where no crops were planted.

es.L: Ve y proclama a los oídos de Jerusalén, diciendo: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q Me acuerdo de ti, del amor leal de tu juventud, \q del amor de tus días de novia, \q de cuando andabas en pos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} en el desierto, \q en una tierra no sembrada.
es.B: Ve y grita de modo que Jerusalén lo oiga: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: \q Recuerdo el amor fiel de tu juventud, \q cómo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} amabas como una novia, \q cómo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} seguías por el desierto, \q por una tierra donde nada se sembraba.
es.R: Ve y anuncia esto a la gente de Jerusalén. Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q Recuerdo el amor fiel que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mostrabas cuando eras joven. \q Como una novia, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} amabas. \q Por el desierto {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} seguiste, \q por una tierra donde no se plantaba nada.

fr.L: Va et crie aux oreilles de Jérusalem, en disant : Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : \q Je me souviens pour toi de l’amour loyal de ta jeunesse, \q de l’amour de tes fiançailles, \q quand tu marchais derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} dans le désert, \q dans une terre non ensemencée.
fr.B: Va crier pour que Jérusalem l’entende : {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : \q Je me souviens de l’amour fidèle de ta jeunesse, \q de ton amour de jeune mariée, \q quand tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivais à travers le désert, \q à travers une terre où rien n’était semé.
fr.R: Va annoncer ceci aux habitants de Jérusalem. Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : \q Je me souviens de l’amour fidèle que tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as montré dans ta jeunesse. \q Tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimais comme une jeune mariée. \q Tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as suivi à travers le désert, \q dans une terre où l’on ne cultivait rien.

sw.L: Nenda ukatangaze masikioni mwa Yerusalemu, ukisema, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: \q Ninakukumbukia upendo usiokoma wa ujana wako, \q upendo wa siku za uchumba wako, \q kunifuata kwako nyikani, \q katika nchi isiyopandwa.
sw.B: Nenda ukapaze sauti ili Yerusalemu isikie: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: \q Ninakumbuka upendo usiokoma wa ujana wako, \q jinsi ulivyonipenda kama bibi arusi, \q jinsi ulivyonifuata jangwani, \q katika nchi ambayo hakuna kilichopandwa.
sw.R: Nenda ukawatangazie watu wa Yerusalemu ujumbe huu. Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: \q Ninakumbuka upendo usiokoma ulionionyesha ulipokuwa kijana. \q Ulinipenda kama bibi arusi. \q Ulinifuata jangwani, \q katika nchi ambayo hakuna mazao yaliyopandwa.

decisions.choice: the loyal love of your youth: Israel's devotion to God in its early days
alternatives: the kindness I showed you in your youth
decisions.reason: The word *hesed* is the loyal, committed love that keeps faith within a bond. Here it is Israel's love for God in the days after the exodus, set beside "the love of your bridal days" and "your walking after me" (compare Hosea 6:4, 6, where God asks for this love from his people). The phrase could also be read as God remembering the kindness he showed Israel in its youth, but the lines that follow all describe what Israel did.

decisions.choice: your bridal days: the time of betrothal and wedding
decisions.reason: The rare word means the state of being a bride, the time of engagement and marriage. The covenant made at Sinai is pictured as a wedding, and Israel as a young bride gladly following her husband (3:1-14; Hosea 2:16-17; Ezekiel 16:8).

decisions.choice: walking after me in the wilderness, in a land not sown: the forty years after the exodus
decisions.reason: "Walk after" is the language of loyal following (Deuteronomy 13:5). The wilderness was a land where nothing could be planted (Deuteronomy 8:2, 15), and Israel followed God there trusting him for everything. Later in the chapter the same verb is used of walking after worthless gods (verses 5, 8, 23, 25).

decisions.choice: I remember for you: I remember to your credit
decisions.reason: The small word "for you" can mean "concerning you" or "in your favor". God holds Israel's early love in memory, and it makes what follows the more painful.

decisions.choice: loyal love (Literal, Balanced); faithful love (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *hesed* in the prophets, as in Isaiah. Readable adds "you showed me" to make clear whose love is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); The LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable); call out so that Jerusalem hears
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the messenger formula. "Proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem" is said at Balanced as "call out so that Jerusalem hears" and at Readable as "announce this to the people of Jerusalem".

decisions.choice: "Así dice el SEÑOR:" (L); "El SEÑOR dice esto:" (B); "Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR:" (R); oracles without quotation marks
decisions.reason: The messenger formula as the terms note sets it for Spanish. As in the English, God's speech in the oracles takes no quotation marks; Jerusalem is addressed as a woman, "tú", with feminine agreement.

decisions.choice: "amor leal" (L, B); "amor fiel" (R)
decisions.reason: Hesed as the Psalms note sets it for Spanish.

decisions.choice: BWANA asema hivi: (Literal); Hivi ndivyo BWANA asemavyo: (Balanced); Hili ndilo BWANA analosema: (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording of "Thus says the LORD" in Swahili, as 2 Kings 19:6 and the terms note; the oracle that follows takes no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: upendo usiokoma
decisions.reason: Hesed is "upendo usiokoma" at every level, as the published Psalms; the English Readable's "faithful love" is the same sense.

decisions.choice: "l’amour loyal" (L); "l’amour fidèle" (B, R), for *hesed* in the whole book
decisions.reason: The wording of the French Psalms for *hesed*. The English keeps "loyal love" at Balanced too; French Balanced follows its own Psalms, where "amour fidèle" is the natural phrase.

decisions.choice: "tu" for Jerusalem and Israel addressed as a woman, "vous" for the people addressed in the plural, following the Hebrew's number through the book
decisions.reason: The Hebrew switches between feminine singular (the city or the nation pictured as a wife) and masculine plural (the people); French follows each switch, with feminine agreement for the woman ("tu t’es souillée").

source.text: קֹ֤דֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַיהוָ֔ה רֵאשִׁ֖ית תְּבוּאָתֹ֑הכָּל־אֹכְלָ֣יו יֶאְשָׁ֔מוּ רָעָ֛ה תָּבֹ֥א אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Holiness [was] Israel to Yahweh, [the] firstfruits of his harvest; all devouring it would be held guilty; disaster would come to them, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Israel [was] holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the firstfruits of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest; \q all who devoured it were held guilty; \q disaster came upon them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Israel was set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the first share of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest. \q Whoever ate of it was held guilty, \q and disaster came on them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The people of Israel belonged to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone. \q They were like the first part of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest. \q Anyone who tried to harm them was guilty, \q and disaster came on them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Santo [era] Israel para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q las primicias de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cosecha; \q todos los que lo devoraban eran culpables; \q la desgracia venía sobre ellos, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Israel estaba consagrado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, \q era la primera parte de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cosecha. \q Quien comía de ella se hacía culpable, \q y la desgracia caía sobre él, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: El pueblo de Israel pertenecía solo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q Era como la primera parte de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cosecha. \q Cualquiera que intentaba hacerle daño era culpable, \q y la desgracia caía sobre él, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Israël [était] sainteté pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q les prémices de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} récolte ; \q tous ceux qui le dévoraient se rendaient coupables ; \q le malheur venait sur eux, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Israël était mis à part comme saint pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q la première part de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} récolte. \q Quiconque en mangeait se rendait coupable, \q et le malheur s’abattait sur lui, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Le peuple d’Israël appartenait {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} seul. \q Il était comme la première part de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} récolte. \q Tous ceux qui voulaient lui faire du mal étaient coupables, \q et le malheur s’abattait sur eux, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Israeli [alikuwa] mtakatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q malimbuko ya mavuno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}; \q wote waliomla walihesabiwa kuwa na hatia; \q mabaya yaliwajia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Israeli alitengwa kuwa mtakatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q fungu la kwanza la mavuno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Yeyote aliyekula sehemu yake alihesabiwa kuwa na hatia, \q na maafa yakamjia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Watu wa Israeli walikuwa mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} peke yake. \q Walikuwa kama sehemu ya kwanza ya mavuno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Yeyote aliyejaribu kuwadhuru alikuwa na hatia, \q na maafa yakamjia, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: holy ... the firstfruits of his harvest: set apart as God's own
decisions.reason: The first of every harvest belonged to God and was holy; only the priests might eat it, and anyone else who ate a holy thing was guilty (Exodus 23:19; Leviticus 22:10-16; Numbers 18:12-13). Israel is pictured as God's own firstfruits, so whoever attacked it was eating what belonged to him.

decisions.choice: devoured it ... held guilty: those who preyed on Israel bore the guilt
decisions.reason: The verb "devour" is used of nations that destroy Israel (10:25; 30:16), and the verb for guilt is the one used of eating a holy thing by mistake (Leviticus 5:17-19). The enemies who fed on Israel were treated as guilty of taking what was God's.

decisions.choice: were held guilty ... came: what used to happen in Israel's early days
decisions.reason: The verbs have the form often used for something that happened again and again in the past. The verse still speaks of the days of verse 2, when God guarded his people.

decisions.choice: belonged to the LORD alone ... tried to harm them
decisions.reason: Readable says what "holy" means here, belonging only to God, and puts the picture of eating God's firstfruits as harming his people (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (Literal, Balanced); says the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula in the prophets.

decisions.choice: malimbuko
decisions.reason: "Malimbuko", the first part of a harvest given to God, is the Pentateuch's word for the firstfruits; Balanced and Readable say "the first share/part".

source.text: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְכָֽל־מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear [the] word of Yahweh, house of Jacob, and all [the] clans of [the] house of Israel.

en.L: Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, house of Jacob, \q and all the clans of the house of Israel.
en.B: Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, house of Jacob, \q all you clans of the house of Israel.
en.R: Listen to the message of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you descendants of Jacob, \q all you families of the people of Israel.

es.L: {{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, casa de Jacob, \q y todas las familias de la casa de Israel.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, casa de Jacob, \q todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, clanes de la casa de Israel.
es.R: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} este mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, descendientes de Jacob, \q todas las familias del pueblo de Israel.

fr.L: Écoutez la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, maison de Jacob, \q et tous les clans de la maison d’Israël.
fr.B: Écoutez la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, maison de Jacob, \q vous tous, clans de la maison d’Israël.
fr.R: Écoutez le message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, descendants de Jacob, \q vous toutes, familles du peuple d’Israël.

sw.L: Sikieni neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nyumba ya Yakobo, \q na koo zote za nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.B: Sikilizeni neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, enyi nyumba ya Yakobo, \q enyi koo zote za nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.R: Sikilizeni ujumbe huu kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, enyi wazao wa Yakobo, \q enyi jamaa zote za watu wa Israeli.

decisions.choice: house of Jacob ... house of Israel: the whole people descended from Jacob
decisions.reason: Jacob was given the name Israel (Genesis 32:29), and his descendants are his "house", his family. The northern kingdom had fallen a century before Jeremiah; the words are spoken to Jerusalem (verse 2), whose people are addressed as the heirs of all Israel and its history.

decisions.choice: clans: the family groups that made up the tribes
decisions.reason: The word names the large family groups within each tribe (Numbers 26). "All the clans" means every part of the nation, not one group only.

decisions.choice: descendants of Jacob ... families of the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable explains "house" as "descendants" and "people", and says "families" for clans.

decisions.choice: "Oigan"/"Oíd" (L); "Escuchen"/"Escuchad" (B, R); every plural "you" in a plural_you span
decisions.reason: The people are addressed as a group, so every plural "you", verb, pronoun or possessive, takes the plural you setting: Latin American forms by default, the forms of Spain as the alternative. "Hear the word of the LORD" keeps the terms note's wording at each level.

decisions.choice: Sikieni neno la BWANA (Literal); Sikilizeni neno la BWANA (Balanced); Sikilizeni ujumbe huu kutoka kwa BWANA (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording of "Hear the word of the LORD", as 2 Kings 20:16 and the terms note.

decisions.choice: "Écoutez la parole du SEIGNEUR" (L, B); "Écoutez le message du SEIGNEUR" (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The call to hear the LORD's word keeps one wording at each level; Readable says "message", as in its formula "m’a donné ce message".

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה מַה־מָּצְא֨וּ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֥ם בִּי֙ עָ֔וֶל כִּ֥י רָחֲק֖וּ מֵעָלָ֑י וַיֵּֽלְכ֛וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י הַהֶ֖בֶל וַיֶּהְבָּֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: What did they find, your fathers, in me [of] injustice, that they went far from me and walked after the vanity and became vain?

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: What injustice did your fathers find in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q that they went far from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and went after worthless idols and became worthless?
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: What did your ancestors find wrong in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q that they went so far from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and went after worthless idols and became worthless themselves?
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Your ancestors must have thought I had wronged them. \q Why else would they go so far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q They followed useless idols and became useless themselves.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: ¿Qué injusticia hallaron en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}, \q que se alejaron de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} \q y anduvieron tras ídolos vanos, y se volvieron vanos?
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: ¿Qué mal encontraron en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}, \q para alejarse tanto de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} \q y seguir ídolos vanos, y volverse vanos ellos mismos?
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: {{plural_you:Sus antepasados|Vuestros antepasados}} debieron pensar que yo los había tratado mal. \q ¿Por qué otra razón se habrían alejado tanto de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}? \q Siguieron ídolos inútiles y se volvieron inútiles ellos mismos.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Quelle injustice vos pères ont-ils trouvée en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q pour s’éloigner de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} \q et marcher derrière la vanité et devenir vains ?
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Qu’ont trouvé vos ancêtres à {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reprocher, \q pour s’éloigner tant de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q pour suivre des idoles vaines et devenir vains eux-mêmes ?
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Vos ancêtres ont dû penser que je leur avais fait du tort. \q Sinon, pourquoi seraient-ils partis si loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ? \q Ils ont suivi des idoles inutiles et ils sont devenus inutiles eux-mêmes.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Baba zenu waliona uovu gani ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q hata wakaenda mbali nami, \q wakafuata sanamu zisizofaa kitu, wakawa watu wasiofaa kitu?
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Babu zenu waliona kosa gani kwangu, \q hata wakaenda mbali nami hivyo, \q wakafuata sanamu zisizofaa kitu, nao wenyewe wakawa hawafai kitu?
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Huenda babu zenu walidhani kwamba niliwakosea. \q La sivyo, kwa nini walikwenda mbali nami hivyo? \q Walifuata sanamu zisizo na faida, nao wenyewe wakawa hawana faida.

decisions.choice: injustice: a wrong done, as if God had dealt unfairly with them
decisions.reason: The word means unfairness or wrongdoing. The Song of Moses calls God "a God of faithfulness and without injustice" (Deuteronomy 32:4), using the same word. The question is the opening of God's case against his people (verse 9): they left him, though he had done them no wrong (compare Micah 6:3).

decisions.choice: went after worthless idols and became worthless: people become like what they worship
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb are the same word: they followed *hevel* (a breath, something empty) and became *hevel*. 2 Kings 17:15 says the same of the northern kingdom in the same words, and Psalm 115:8 says that those who make idols become like them.

decisions.choice: your fathers: the generations of Israel since the exodus
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the people's ancestors as a whole, from the generation that settled in the land to Jeremiah's day (verse 7; 7:25-26).

decisions.choice: worthless idols ... became worthless (Literal, Balanced); useless idols ... became useless (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 17:15, which has the same phrase. Each level repeats one word so that the play between noun and verb is kept (m2).

decisions.choice: Your ancestors must have thought I had wronged them. Why else ...?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the bitter question into a statement and a second question, so that a young reader hears its point: God had done nothing to deserve being left.

decisions.choice: "ídolos vanos ... se volvieron vanos" (L, B); "ídolos inútiles ... se volvieron inútiles" (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish keeps the one word for the idols and for what their worshipers became, as the English does, so the play on hevel stays.

decisions.choice: sanamu zisizofaa kitu ... wasiofaa kitu (Literal, Balanced); sanamu zisizo na faida ... hawana faida (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same Swahili word is used for the idols and for what their worshipers became, as the Hebrew uses one word (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "la vanité ... devenir vains" (L); "des idoles vaines ... devenir vains" (B); "des idoles inutiles ... devenus inutiles" (R)
decisions.reason: Each level repeats one word for the noun and the verb, so the play is kept (m2): people become like what they worship.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR :" (L); "Le SEIGNEUR dit ceci :" (B); "Voici ce que dit le SEIGNEUR :" (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The messenger formula of 2 Kings 19:6 and 20:1, one wording per level; the oracle that follows takes no quotation marks.

source.text: וְלֹ֣א אָמְר֔וּ אַיֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה הַמַּעֲלֶ֥ה אֹתָ֖נוּ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הַמּוֹלִ֨יךְ אֹתָ֜נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר בְּאֶ֨רֶץ עֲרָבָ֤ה וְשׁוּחָה֙ בְּאֶ֨רֶץ֙ צִיָּ֣ה וְצַלְמָ֔וֶת בְּאֶ֗רֶץ לֹֽא־עָ֤בַר בָּהּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יָשַׁ֥ב אָדָ֖ם שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And not they said, Where [is] Yahweh, the [one] bringing up us from [the] land of Egypt, the [one] leading us in the wilderness, in a land of desert and pit, in a land of drought and deep darkness, in a land not passed through it anyone, and not dwelt a human there?

en.L: And they did not say, "Where [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q who brought us up from the land of Egypt, \q who led us in the wilderness, \q in a land of desert and pit, \q in a land of drought and deep darkness, \q in a land that no one passed through, and where no human lived?"
en.B: They did not ask, "Where is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the one who brought us up from Egypt's land, \q who guided us in the wilderness, \q through a land of desert plains and pits, \q a land of drought and deep darkness, \q a land no one crosses and no one lives in?"
en.R: They never asked, "Where is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? \q He brought us up out of Egypt. \q He led us through the desert, \q through dry land full of pits, \q a dry and dark land, \q where no one travels and no one lives."

es.L: Y no dijeron: «¿Dónde [está] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q que nos hizo subir de la tierra de Egipto, \q que nos condujo por el desierto, \q por una tierra de llanuras desiertas y de hoyos, \q por una tierra de sequía y de densa oscuridad, \q por una tierra por la que nadie pasaba y donde no habitaba ningún ser humano?».
es.B: No preguntaron: «¿Dónde está {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q el que nos sacó de la tierra de Egipto, \q el que nos guio por el desierto, \q por una tierra de llanuras áridas y de hoyos, \q una tierra de sequía y de densa oscuridad, \q una tierra que nadie cruza y donde nadie vive?».
es.R: Nunca preguntaron: «¿Dónde está {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}? \q Él nos sacó de Egipto. \q Nos guio por el desierto, \q por una tierra seca y llena de hoyos, \q una tierra seca y oscura, \q por donde nadie viaja y donde nadie vive».

fr.L: Et ils n’ont pas dit : « Où [est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q qui nous a fait monter du pays d’Égypte, \q qui nous a conduits dans le désert, \q dans un pays de steppe et de fosses, \q dans un pays de sécheresse et d’ombre de mort, \q dans un pays où personne ne passe et où aucun homme n’habite ? »
fr.B: Ils n’ont pas demandé : « Où est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q celui qui nous a fait monter du pays d’Égypte, \q qui nous a guidés dans le désert, \q à travers un pays de steppes et de crevasses, \q un pays de sécheresse et de ténèbres épaisses, \q un pays que personne ne traverse et où personne n’habite ? »
fr.R: Ils n’ont jamais demandé : « Où est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? \q Il nous a fait sortir d’Égypte. \q Il nous a conduits à travers le désert, \q à travers une terre sèche pleine de trous, \q une terre aride et sombre, \q où personne ne passe et où personne n’habite. »

sw.L: Wala hawakusema, "Yuko wapi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q aliyetupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri, \q aliyetuongoza nyikani, \q katika nchi ya jangwa na mashimo, \q katika nchi ya ukame na giza kuu, \q katika nchi ambayo hakuna mtu aliyepita ndani yake, wala hakuna mwanadamu aliyekaa humo?"
sw.B: Hawakuuliza, "Yuko wapi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q yule aliyetupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri, \q aliyetuongoza nyikani, \q katika nchi ya nyika na mashimo, \q nchi ya ukame na giza kuu, \q nchi ambayo hakuna mtu anayeivuka wala anayeishi ndani yake?"
sw.R: Hawakuuliza kamwe, "Yuko wapi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}? \q Alitutoa Misri. \q Alituongoza jangwani, \q katika nchi kavu iliyojaa mashimo, \q nchi kavu yenye giza, \q ambako hakuna mtu anayesafiri wala anayeishi."

decisions.choice: Where is Yahweh?: a question of people seeking God
decisions.reason: To ask "Where is the LORD?" is to look for him and call on him, as Elisha did when he struck the Jordan (2 Kings 2:14; Job 35:10). Their ancestors never went looking for the God who had brought them out of Egypt. The priests did not ask it either (verse 8).

decisions.choice: deep darkness: thick gloom, a place of danger
decisions.reason: The word means deep darkness. Older versions took it as two words, "shadow of death", as in Psalm 23:4. Here it describes the wilderness as a dark, deadly place where travelers could not see their way.

decisions.choice: brought us up ... led us in the wilderness: the exodus and the journey through the desert
decisions.reason: The words recall how Moses described the wilderness, "the great and terrible wilderness" with its thirst and its dangers (Deuteronomy 8:15; 32:10). God brought Israel through a land where no one could live.

decisions.choice: they did not ask / they never asked
decisions.reason: The verb is "say"; Balanced and Readable say "ask" because what follows is a question.

decisions.choice: Where is the LORD? He brought us up ... He led us ...
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long question into short sentences. "He" begins each sentence and so has no capital-letter setting.

decisions.choice: "l’ombre de mort"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional rendering of *tsalmavet*, which the English renders "deep darkness"; Balanced says "ténèbres épaisses".

source.text: וָאָבִ֤יא אֶתְכֶם֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל לֶאֱכֹ֥ל פִּרְיָ֖הּ וְטוּבָ֑הּ וַתָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ וַתְּטַמְּא֣וּ אֶת־אַרְצִ֔י וְנַחֲלָתִ֥י שַׂמְתֶּ֖ם לְתוֹעֵבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I brought you into a land of the orchard, to eat its fruit and its good; and you came and you defiled my land, and my inheritance you made into an abomination.

en.L: And I brought you into a land of orchard, \q to eat its fruit and its good things; \q but you came in and defiled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, \q and made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance an abomination.
en.B: I brought you into orchard land, \q to eat its fruit and its good things. \q But you came in and defiled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land; \q you made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance something detestable.
en.R: I brought you into a land full of orchards \q so you could eat its fruit and all its good food. \q But when you came in, you made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land unclean. \q You made the land that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into something I hate.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:los|os}} traje a una tierra de huertos, \q para comer su fruto y sus bienes; \q pero {{plural_you:entraron y contaminaron|entrasteis y contaminasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra, \q e hicieron de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} heredad una abominación.
es.B: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} traje a una tierra de huertos, \q para que {{plural_you:comieran|comierais}} su fruto y sus bienes. \q Pero {{plural_you:entraron y contaminaron|entrasteis y contaminasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra; \q {{plural_you:convirtieron|convertisteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} heredad en algo detestable.
es.R: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} traje a una tierra llena de huertos \q para que {{plural_you:comieran|comierais}} sus frutos y todo lo bueno que da. \q Pero cuando {{plural_you:entraron|entrasteis}}, {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} impura {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra. \q {{plural_you:Convirtieron|Convertisteis}} la tierra que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece en algo que yo detesto.

fr.L: Et je vous ai fait entrer dans un pays de vergers, \q pour en manger le fruit et les biens ; \q mais vous êtes entrés et vous avez souillé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays, \q et de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} héritage vous avez fait une abomination.
fr.B: Je vous ai fait entrer dans un pays de vergers, \q pour que vous en mangiez les fruits et les bonnes choses. \q Mais vous êtes entrés et vous avez souillé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays ; \q de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} héritage, vous avez fait une chose détestable.
fr.R: Je vous ai fait entrer dans un pays plein de vergers, \q pour que vous puissiez manger ses fruits et toutes ses bonnes choses. \q Mais quand vous êtes arrivés, vous avez rendu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays impur. \q Le pays qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartient, vous en avez fait une chose que je déteste.

sw.L: Nami niliwaleta katika nchi ya bustani, \q mle matunda yake na mema yake; \q lakini mlipoingia mkainajisi nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q na urithi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mkaufanya chukizo.
sw.B: Niliwaleta katika nchi ya bustani za matunda, \q mle matunda yake na mema yake. \q Lakini mlipoingia mliinajisi nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q mliufanya urithi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kuwa kitu cha kuchukiza.
sw.R: Niliwaleta katika nchi iliyojaa bustani za matunda \q ili mle matunda yake na vyakula vyake vyote vizuri. \q Lakini mlipoingia, mliifanya nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuwa najisi. \q Mliifanya nchi iliyo mali {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuwa kitu ninachokichukia.

decisions.choice: the orchard: fruitful garden land
decisions.reason: The word *karmel* means a planted garden or orchard, land rich with fruit trees and vines (Isaiah 10:18; 29:17). It is the opposite of the wilderness of verse 6.

decisions.choice: defiled: made unclean in God's sight
decisions.reason: The verb is the word for ritual uncleanness. The Law warned that idolatry, bloodshed and sexual sin would make the land unclean (Leviticus 18:24-28; Numbers 35:33-34). Jeremiah names both idols and innocent blood later in the chapter (verses 23, 34).

decisions.choice: my inheritance: the land as God's own possession
decisions.reason: The land was God's own, given to Israel to live on (Exodus 15:17; Leviticus 25:23). The people had treated his own property with contempt.

decisions.choice: abomination: something God finds detestable
decisions.reason: The word names what God hates and rejects, above all idols and the worship of other gods (Deuteronomy 7:25-26; 12:31).

decisions.choice: a land of orchard / orchard land / a land full of orchards; abomination / something detestable / something I hate
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *karmel* (as Isaiah). For the abomination Balanced uses a modern word and Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: ninyi (plural "you")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew addresses the people here in the plural (verses 4-13), and Swahili follows it with "ninyi" and the plural verb forms; where the Hebrew speaks to the people in the singular (verse 2, and from verse 14 on, apart from verses 29-31), Swahili uses "wewe".

source.text: הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים לֹ֤א אָֽמְרוּ֙ אַיֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה וְתֹפְשֵׂ֤י הַתּוֹרָה֙ לֹ֣א יְדָע֔וּנִי וְהָרֹעִ֖ים פָּ֣שְׁעוּ בִ֑י וְהַנְּבִיאִים֙ נִבְּא֣וּ בַבַּ֔עַל וְאַחֲרֵ֥י לֹֽא־יוֹעִ֖לוּ הָלָֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: The priests not said, Where [is] Yahweh? And [those] handling the instruction not knew me, and the shepherds rebelled against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal, and after [things that] not profit they walked.

en.L: The priests did not say, "Where [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" \q Those who handle the instruction did not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q the shepherds rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q the prophets prophesied by Baal \q and walked after things that do not profit.
en.B: The priests did not ask, "Where is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" \q Those who handle the instruction did not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q the shepherds rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q the prophets prophesied by Baal \q and followed things that are of no profit.
en.R: The priests never asked, "Where is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" \q Those in charge of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching did not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q The leaders turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q The prophets spoke in the name of Baal \q and followed gods that cannot help anyone.

es.L: Los sacerdotes no dijeron: «¿Dónde [está] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?». \q Los que manejan la instrucción no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocieron; \q los pastores se rebelaron contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; \q los profetas profetizaron por Baal \q y anduvieron tras cosas que no aprovechan.
es.B: Los sacerdotes no preguntaron: «¿Dónde está {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?». \q Los que manejan la instrucción no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocieron; \q los pastores se rebelaron contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; \q los profetas profetizaron por Baal \q y siguieron cosas que no sirven de nada.
es.R: Los sacerdotes nunca preguntaron: «¿Dónde está {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?». \q Los encargados de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enseñanza no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocieron. \q Los dirigentes se volvieron contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Los profetas hablaron en nombre de Baal \q y siguieron a dioses que no pueden ayudar a nadie.

fr.L: Les prêtres n’ont pas dit : « Où [est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? » \q Ceux qui manient la loi ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont pas connu ; \q les bergers se sont révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q les prophètes ont prophétisé par Baal \q et ont marché derrière ce qui ne sert à rien.
fr.B: Les prêtres n’ont pas demandé : « Où est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? » \q Ceux qui manient l’instruction ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont pas connu ; \q les bergers se sont révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q les prophètes ont prophétisé par Baal \q et ont suivi ce qui ne sert à rien.
fr.R: Les prêtres n’ont jamais demandé : « Où est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? » \q Ceux qui étaient chargés de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} enseignement ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont pas connu. \q Les chefs se sont révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q Les prophètes ont parlé au nom de Baal \q et ils ont suivi des dieux qui ne peuvent aider personne.

sw.L: Makuhani hawakusema, "Yuko wapi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?" \q Nao wanaoshika sheria hawakunijua; \q nao wachungaji waliniasi; \q nao manabii walitabiri kwa Baali, \q wakafuata mambo yasiyofaidia.
sw.B: Makuhani hawakuuliza, "Yuko wapi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?" \q Wanaoshughulikia mafundisho hawakunijua; \q wachungaji waliniasi; \q manabii walitabiri kwa jina la Baali, \q wakafuata mambo yasiyo na faida.
sw.R: Makuhani hawakuuliza kamwe, "Yuko wapi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?" \q Wale waliosimamia mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} hawakunijua. \q Viongozi waliniasi. \q Manabii walisema kwa jina la Baali \q na kufuata miungu isiyoweza kumsaidia mtu yeyote.

decisions.choice: those who handle the instruction: the priests who taught God's law
decisions.reason: The priests were to teach Israel God's *torah*, his instruction (Deuteronomy 33:10; Malachi 2:6-7). "Handle" means to hold or deal with it as their own work. Those who handled God's words did not know God himself.

decisions.choice: the shepherds: the kings and rulers
decisions.reason: In Jeremiah and the other prophets "shepherds" are the rulers of the people, who were to care for them as a shepherd for a flock (2 Samuel 5:2; Jeremiah 23:1-4; Ezekiel 34). The verse names the four groups that led the nation: priests, teachers of the law, rulers and prophets.

decisions.choice: prophesied by Baal: spoke in Baal's name
decisions.reason: The prophets claimed Baal as the source of their messages (23:13), as true prophets spoke in Yahweh's name.

decisions.choice: things that do not profit: gods that cannot help
decisions.reason: This is a common description of idols (verse 11; 1 Samuel 12:21; Isaiah 44:9-10). The Hebrew for "they do not profit" may echo the sound of Baal's name.

decisions.choice: instruction (Literal, Balanced), teaching (Readable); shepherds (Literal, Balanced), leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *torah* follows Isaiah. Readable says "leaders" for the shepherd picture (m2) and supplies "my" before teaching, since God is speaking.

decisions.choice: "la instrucción" (L, B), "enseñanza" (R); "pastores" (L, B), "dirigentes" (R)
decisions.reason: Torah as the terms note sets it ("instrucción", "enseñanza"); the shepherds are the rulers, named so at Readable as the English does.

decisions.choice: sheria (Literal); mafundisho (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *Torah* is "sheria" at Literal and "mafundisho" at Balanced and Readable throughout Jeremiah, as the terms note and the Psalms note set; only 31:33 keeps "sheria" at Balanced, after Hebrews 8:10.

decisions.choice: "la loi" (L); "l’instruction" (B); "mon enseignement" (R), for God's *torah* in the whole book
decisions.reason: The French Psalms' word family for *torah*: one word per level, never a legal code. Readable adds "mon", as the English does, since God speaks.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן עֹ֛ד אָרִ֥יב אִתְּכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י בְנֵיכֶ֖ם אָרִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore still I will contend with you, declares Yahweh, and with [the] children of your children I will contend.

en.L: Therefore I will still contend with you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and with your children's children I will contend.
en.B: So I will go on bringing charges against you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and I will bring charges against your children's children.
en.R: So I will keep on taking you to court, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will take your grandchildren to court too.

es.L: Por tanto, aún litigaré con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q y con los hijos de {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} litigaré.
es.B: Por eso seguiré presentando cargos contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q y presentaré cargos contra los hijos de {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}}.
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:los|os}} seguiré llevando a juicio, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q También llevaré a juicio a {{plural_you:sus nietos|vuestros nietos}}.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je plaiderai encore contre vous, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et contre les fils de vos fils je plaiderai.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi je continuerai à porter plainte contre vous, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et je porterai plainte contre les enfants de vos enfants.
fr.R: Alors je vais continuer à vous faire un procès, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Et je ferai aussi un procès à vos petits-enfants.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo bado nitashindana nanyi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q na wana wa wana wenu nitashindana nao.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nitaendelea kuwashtaki, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nami nitawashtaki wana wa wana wenu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nitaendelea kuwapeleka mahakamani, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Nitawapeleka wajukuu wenu mahakamani pia.

decisions.choice: contend: bring a case in court against someone
decisions.reason: The verb *riv* and its noun are the language of a lawsuit: to accuse, to argue a case, to seek a verdict. The prophets often present God as bringing a case against his people for breaking the covenant (Isaiah 3:13; Hosea 4:1; Micah 6:1-2). Verses 5-13 are the charges, with heaven called as witness (verse 12), and in verse 29 the people try to turn the case back on God.

decisions.choice: still: the case goes on
decisions.reason: The word means "still" or "yet again": God has not finished with them. His case reaches to the generations to come, who continue in their fathers' ways (verse 5; Exodus 20:5).

decisions.choice: contend (Literal); bring charges (Balanced); take you to court (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the courtroom picture. Literal uses the general verb, Balanced the language of an accuser, and Readable the plainest form. Verse 29 uses the same wording for the same verb.

decisions.choice: "litigaré" (L); "presentaré cargos" (B); "llevaré a juicio" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the language of a lawsuit; each level follows the English level's wording of it.

decisions.choice: kushindana (Literal); kushtaki (Balanced); kuwapeleka mahakamani (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is a lawsuit (meaning decision m1); each level keeps its word for it in verse 29.

decisions.choice: "plaider contre" (L); "porter plainte contre" (B); "faire un procès" (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the courtroom picture (m1), as the English does; verse 29 uses the same words.

source.text: כִּ֣י עִבְר֞וּ אִיֵּ֤י כִתִּיִּים֙ וּרְא֔וּ וְקֵדָ֛ר שִׁלְח֥וּ וְהִֽתְבּוֹנְנ֖וּ מְאֹ֑ד וּרְא֕וּ הֵ֥ן הָיְתָ֖ה כָּזֹֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: For cross over [to the] coastlands of Kittim and see, and [to] Kedar send and consider very [carefully], and see if there has been like this.

en.L: For cross over to the coastlands of Kittim and see, \q send to Kedar and consider carefully, \q and see if there has been [anything] like this.
en.B: Go over to the coastlands of Kittim and look; \q send to Kedar and think it through with care; \q see whether anything like this has ever happened.
en.R: Sail west to the shores of Cyprus and look. \q Send someone east to Kedar and study it closely. \q See if anything like this has ever happened.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:crucen|cruzad}} a las costas de Quitim y {{plural_you:vean|ved}}, \q {{plural_you:envíen|enviad}} a Cedar y {{plural_you:consideren|considerad}} con cuidado, \q y {{plural_you:vean|ved}} si ha habido [algo] como esto.
es.B: {{plural_you:Pasen|Pasad}} a las costas de Quitim y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}; \q {{plural_you:envíen|enviad}} a alguien a Cedar y {{plural_you:examínenlo|examinadlo}} con atención; \q {{plural_you:vean|ved}} si alguna vez ha sucedido algo así.
es.R: {{plural_you:Naveguen|Navegad}} hacia el oeste, hasta las costas de Chipre, y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}. \q {{plural_you:Envíen|Enviad}} a alguien hacia el este, a Cedar, y {{plural_you:averigüen|averiguad}} bien. \q {{plural_you:Vean|Ved}} si alguna vez ha sucedido algo así.

fr.L: Car passez aux îles de Kittim et voyez, \q envoyez à Kédar et observez bien, \q et voyez s’il y a eu [rien] de pareil.
fr.B: Allez donc aux îles de Kittim et regardez ; \q envoyez quelqu’un à Kédar et examinez avec soin ; \q voyez si pareille chose est jamais arrivée.
fr.R: Prenez la mer vers l’ouest, jusqu’aux côtes de Chypre, et regardez. \q Envoyez quelqu’un vers l’est, jusqu’à Kédar, et observez bien. \q Voyez si une chose pareille est déjà arrivée.

sw.L: Kwa maana vukeni mpaka visiwa vya Kitimu mkaone, \q tumeni [watu] Kedari mkafikiri sana, \q mkaone kama kumekuwa na [jambo] kama hili.
sw.B: Nendeni ng'ambo mpaka pwani za Kitimu mkaangalie; \q tumeni watu Kedari mkalitafakari kwa makini; \q mwone kama jambo kama hili limewahi kutokea.
sw.R: Safirini kwa meli kuelekea magharibi mpaka pwani za Kipro mkaangalie. \q Tumeni mtu mashariki mpaka Kedari akachunguze vizuri. \q Mwone kama jambo kama hili limewahi kutokea.

decisions.choice: Kittim and Kedar: the far west and the far east
decisions.reason: Kittim was the people of Cyprus, and the name came to stand for the lands across the sea to the west (Isaiah 23:1, 12). Kedar was a tribe of the Arabian desert to the east (Genesis 25:13; Isaiah 21:16). Search from one end of the known world to the other.

decisions.choice: see if there has been anything like this: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The search is meant to prove that nothing like Israel's act has ever been done, as verse 11 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: sail west ... Cyprus ... send someone east
decisions.reason: Readable names Kittim as Cyprus, as in Isaiah, and adds the directions, which the names imply (m1).

decisions.choice: "las costas de Quitim" (L, B); "las costas de Chipre" (R); "Cedar"
decisions.reason: Kittim and coastlands as the terms note sets them for Spanish; Readable names Cyprus and the directions, as the English does.

decisions.choice: visiwa vya Kitimu (Literal); pwani za Kitimu (Balanced); pwani za Kipro (Readable); Kedari
decisions.reason: Iyyim and Kittim are worded as the terms note sets them; Readable says Cyprus ("Kipro", as Acts) as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "les îles de Kittim" (L, B); "les côtes de Chypre" (R); "Kédar"
decisions.reason: *Iyyim* is "les îles" in the prophets; Readable names Kittim as Cyprus, as the English does.

source.text: הַהֵימִ֥יר גּוֹי֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְהֵ֖מָּה לֹ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַמִּ֛י הֵמִ֥יר כְּבוֹד֖וֹ בְּל֥וֹא יוֹעִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: Has exchanged a nation gods, and they [are] not gods? But my people has exchanged its glory for [what] not profits.

en.L: Has a nation exchanged gods, \q even though they [are] not gods? \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have exchanged their glory for what does not profit.
en.B: Has any nation ever exchanged its gods, \q even though they are not gods at all? \q Yet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have exchanged their glory for something that gives no help.
en.R: No nation has ever traded its gods for new ones, \q and their gods are not even real gods. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have traded {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, their glory, for gods that cannot help them.

es.L: ¿Ha cambiado una nación [sus] dioses, \q aunque ellos no [son] dioses? \q Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo ha cambiado su gloria por lo que no aprovecha.
es.B: ¿Ha cambiado alguna nación sus dioses, \q aunque ni siquiera son dioses? \q Sin embargo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo ha cambiado su gloria por algo que no sirve de nada.
es.R: Ninguna nación ha cambiado nunca a sus dioses por otros, \q y eso que sus dioses ni siquiera son dioses de verdad. \q Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha cambiado a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, su gloria, por dioses que no pueden ayudarlos.

fr.L: Une nation a-t-elle changé de dieux, \q alors qu’ils ne [sont] pas des dieux ? \q Mais {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple a échangé sa gloire contre ce qui ne sert à rien.
fr.B: Une nation a-t-elle jamais changé de dieux, \q alors que ce ne sont même pas des dieux ? \q Et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple a échangé sa gloire contre ce qui n’apporte aucune aide !
fr.R: Aucune nation n’a jamais échangé ses dieux contre d’autres, \q et pourtant leurs dieux ne sont même pas de vrais dieux. \q Mais {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a échangé, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui suis sa gloire, contre des dieux qui ne peuvent pas l’aider.

sw.L: Je, taifa limewahi kubadili miungu, \q ingawa hiyo si miungu? \q Lakini watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wameubadili utukufu wao kwa kisichofaidia.
sw.B: Je, kuna taifa lolote lililowahi kubadili miungu yake, \q ingawa hiyo si miungu kamwe? \q Lakini watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wameubadili utukufu wao kwa kitu kisicho na msaada.
sw.R: Hakuna taifa lililowahi kuibadili miungu yake kwa miungu mipya, \q na miungu yao si miungu ya kweli hata kidogo. \q Lakini watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wamenibadili {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, utukufu wao, kwa miungu isiyoweza kuwasaidia.

decisions.choice: their glory: God himself, in whom their honor lay
decisions.reason: Israel's glory was the God who lived among them and made them great. Psalm 106:20 says the same of the golden calf: "they exchanged their glory for the image of an ox". To trade him for idols was the strangest of all bargains.

decisions.choice: their glory: the text as written
decisions.reason: Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among a few places where scribes are said to have changed a word out of reverence, here from "my glory" to "their glory" ("its glory"), so as not to write that people exchanged God's glory. The sense is much the same either way.

decisions.choice: and they are not gods: even false gods are kept
decisions.reason: The nations do not abandon even gods who are not gods at all; Israel abandoned the true God (compare 16:20).

decisions.choice: traded me, their glory
decisions.reason: Readable names God as Israel's glory (m1) so that the picture is clear.

source.text: שֹׁ֥מּוּ שָׁמַ֖יִם עַל־זֹ֑את וְשַׂעֲר֛וּ חָרְב֥וּ מְאֹ֖ד נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Be appalled, heavens, at this, and shudder, be dried up very, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Be appalled, heavens, at this; \q shudder, be utterly dried up, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Be horrified at this, you heavens; \q shudder and be utterly stunned, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Sky above, be shocked at this! \q Shake with horror and be completely stunned, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:Espántense|Espantaos}}, cielos, de esto; \q {{plural_you:estremézcanse, quédense|estremeceos, quedaos}} completamente secos, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Horrorícense|Horrorizaos}} de esto, cielos; \q {{plural_you:tiemblen y queden|temblad y quedad}} totalmente pasmados, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: ¡Cielo, asómbrate de esto! \q Tiembla de horror y quédate completamente pasmado, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Soyez stupéfaits de cela, cieux ; \q frissonnez, soyez entièrement desséchés, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Cieux, soyez saisis d’horreur devant cela ; \q frissonnez, restez frappés de stupeur, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Ciel, sois choqué par cela ! \q Tremble d’horreur, reste muet de stupeur, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Shangaeni, enyi mbingu, kwa hili, \q tetemekeni, mkauke kabisa, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Ogopeni kwa hili, enyi mbingu; \q tetemekeni na kupigwa na bumbuazi kabisa, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Enyi mbingu, shtukeni kwa jambo hili! \q Tetemekeni kwa hofu na kushangaa kabisa, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: heavens: called as witnesses to the case
decisions.reason: Heaven and earth were witnesses of the covenant (Deuteronomy 30:19; 32:1), and the prophets summon them when God brings his case against his people (Isaiah 1:2; Micah 6:1-2).

decisions.choice: be utterly dried up: be laid waste with horror
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to be dry or laid waste. Here it is set beside "be appalled" and "shudder", so it means to be overwhelmed and devastated by what has happened. Some take it as "be utterly desolate".

decisions.choice: be utterly stunned / be completely stunned
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the image (m2), since "be dried up" would sound strange said to the sky.

decisions.choice: "Espántense"/"Espantaos", cielos (L, B); "Cielo, asómbrate" (R)
decisions.reason: The heavens are called as witnesses; Literal and Balanced address them in the plural with the plural you setting, Readable speaks to the sky in the singular, as the English Readable does.

source.text: כִּֽי־שְׁתַּ֥יִם רָע֖וֹת עָשָׂ֣ה עַמִּ֑י אֹתִ֨י עָזְב֜וּ מְק֣וֹר׀מַ֣יִם חַיִּ֗ים לַחְצֹ֤ב לָהֶם֙ בֹּאר֔וֹת בֹּארֹת֙ נִשְׁבָּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יָכִ֖לוּ הַמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: For two evils has done my people: me they have forsaken, [the] spring of waters living, to hew for themselves cisterns, cisterns broken, which not can hold the water.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have done two evils: \q they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the spring of living waters, \q to hew out cisterns for themselves, \q broken cisterns that cannot hold the water.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have committed two evils: \q they have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the spring of living water, \q and cut out cisterns for themselves, \q cracked cisterns that can hold no water.
en.R: My people have done two evil things. \q They have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the spring of fresh, flowing water. \q Then they dug out their own pits to store water, \q but the pits are cracked and cannot hold any water.

es.L: Porque dos males ha hecho {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo: \q {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han abandonado a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, fuente de aguas vivas, \q para cavarse cisternas, \q cisternas rotas que no pueden retener el agua.
es.B: Porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo ha cometido dos males: \q {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han abandonado a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, la fuente de agua viva, \q y se han cavado cisternas, \q cisternas agrietadas que no retienen el agua.
es.R: Mi pueblo ha hecho dos cosas malas. \q Ellos {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dejaron a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, el manantial de agua fresca que siempre corre. \q Luego cavaron sus propios pozos para guardar agua, \q pero los pozos están agrietados y no pueden retener nada de agua.

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple a commis deux maux : \q ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont abandonné, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, la source des eaux vives, \q pour se creuser des citernes, \q des citernes fissurées, qui ne retiennent pas l’eau.
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple a commis deux fautes : \q ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont abandonné, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, la source d’eau vive, \q et ils se sont taillé des citernes, \q des citernes lézardées qui ne peuvent garder aucune eau.
fr.R: Mon peuple a fait deux choses mauvaises. \q Ils se sont détournés de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, la source d’eau fraîche qui coule toujours. \q Puis ils ont creusé leurs propres réservoirs pour garder l’eau de pluie, \q mais ces réservoirs sont fendus et ne gardent pas l’eau.

sw.L: Kwa maana watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wamefanya maovu mawili: \q wameniacha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, chemchemi ya maji ya uzima, \q wajichongee visima, \q visima vilivyobomoka, visivyoweza kuyaweka maji.
sw.B: Kwa maana watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wametenda maovu mawili: \q wameniacha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, chemchemi ya maji yaliyo hai, \q wakajichimbia mabirika, \q mabirika yenye nyufa yasiyoweza kuweka maji.
sw.R: Watu wangu wamefanya mambo mawili mabaya. \q Wamegeuka na kuniacha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, chemchemi ya maji safi yanayotiririka. \q Kisha wakajichimbia mashimo yao wenyewe ya kuhifadhia maji, \q lakini mashimo hayo yana nyufa na hayawezi kuweka maji hata kidogo.

decisions.choice: spring of living water ... broken cisterns: running water against stored rainwater
decisions.reason: "Living water" is fresh water that flows from a spring. A cistern was a pit cut into the rock and plastered to catch rainwater for the dry season; its water went stale, and if the rock or plaster cracked it drained away. In a dry land no one would leave a running spring for a leaking cistern.

decisions.choice: me, the spring of living water: God as the source of life
decisions.reason: God himself is the spring (17:13; Psalm 36:10). The people's first evil was to leave him; the second was to make their own sources of help, the idols of verses 5-11 and the foreign powers of verse 18, which can give them nothing.

decisions.choice: two evils: forsaking and replacing
decisions.reason: The two evils are named in turn: leaving the spring, and digging cisterns. The second is not a lesser fault; it shows how foolish the first was.

decisions.choice: fresh, flowing water ... pits to store water
decisions.reason: Readable explains "living water" and "cisterns" (m1). It keeps "spring" so that the picture of God as the source stays.

decisions.choice: maji ya uzima (Literal); maji yaliyo hai (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Living water" is running spring water; Literal keeps the word "uzima" of John 4:10, Balanced says plainly that the water is alive, flowing (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "eaux vives" (L); "eau vive" (B); "eau fraîche qui coule toujours" (R)
decisions.reason: "Eau vive" is the ordinary French for running water from a spring, and keeps the picture of God as the source of life (m2); Readable explains it, as the English does.

source.text: הַעֶ֨בֶד֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־יְלִ֥יד בַּ֖יִת ה֑וּא מַדּ֖וּעַ הָיָ֥ה לָבַֽז׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] a slave Israel? Or one born of [the] house [is] he? Why has he become plunder?

en.L: Is Israel a slave? \q Or is he [a slave] born in the house? \q Why has he become plunder?
en.B: Is Israel a slave? \q Was he born a slave in his master's house? \q Then why has he become plunder?
en.R: Is Israel a slave? \q Was he born into slavery? \q Then why have enemies carried him off like loot?

es.L: ¿Es Israel un esclavo? \q ¿O es [un esclavo] nacido en casa? \q ¿Por qué ha llegado a ser botín?
es.B: ¿Es Israel un esclavo? \q ¿Nació esclavo en la casa de su amo? \q Entonces, ¿por qué ha llegado a ser botín?
es.R: ¿Es Israel un esclavo? \q ¿Nació en la esclavitud? \q Entonces, ¿por qué sus enemigos se lo han llevado como un botín?

fr.L: Israël est-il un esclave ? \q Ou est-il [un esclave] né dans la maison ? \q Pourquoi est-il devenu une proie ?
fr.B: Israël est-il un esclave ? \q Est-il né esclave dans la maison de son maître ? \q Alors pourquoi est-il devenu une proie ?
fr.R: Israël est-il un esclave ? \q Est-il né esclave ? \q Alors pourquoi des ennemis l’ont-ils emporté comme un butin ?

sw.L: Je, Israeli ni mtumwa? \q Au yeye ni [mtumwa] aliyezaliwa nyumbani? \q Mbona amekuwa mateka?
sw.B: Je, Israeli ni mtumwa? \q Je, alizaliwa mtumwa katika nyumba ya bwana wake? \q Basi mbona amekuwa nyara?
sw.R: Je, Israeli ni mtumwa? \q Je, alizaliwa katika utumwa? \q Basi mbona maadui wamemchukua kama nyara?

decisions.choice: one born in the house: a slave born into the household
decisions.reason: A child born to slaves in a household belonged to the master from birth and for life (Genesis 17:12; Leviticus 22:11). Such a person had no family or land to defend him.

decisions.choice: Is Israel a slave? ... Why ...?: questions that expect the answer no
decisions.reason: Israel was not a slave but God's own son (Exodus 4:22) and his firstfruits (verse 3). Yet it is being carried off like the goods of someone with no protector. The answer comes in verse 17: Israel brought this on itself.

decisions.choice: slave at every level
decisions.reason: The word *'eved* is "slave" at every level here, because the point is slavery itself: being owned, set against being a free son of the household.

decisions.choice: Then why ...? / enemies carried him off like loot
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "then" to show the link between the questions, and Readable says who takes the plunder.

decisions.choice: mtumwa
decisions.reason: Slavery itself is the point, so "mtumwa" stands at every level, as the English "slave".

decisions.choice: "esclave" at every level
decisions.reason: The point is slavery itself, set against a free son of the household, so French says "esclave" at every level, as the English does.

source.text: עָלָיו֙ יִשְׁאֲג֣וּ כְפִרִ֔ים נָתְנ֖וּ קוֹלָ֑ם וַיָּשִׁ֤יתוּ אַרְצוֹ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרָ֥יו נִצְּת֖וּ מִבְּלִ֥י יֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: Against him roar young lions, they have given their voice; and they have made his land into a waste; his cities are burned, without inhabitant.

en.L: Against him young lions have roared, \q they have raised their voice; \q they have made his land a waste; \q his cities are burned, without inhabitant.
en.B: Young lions have roared against him; \q they have raised their voices. \q They have made his land a ruin; \q his towns are burned, with no one living there.
en.R: Enemies have roared at him like young lions. \q They have made his land a wasteland. \q His towns have been burned down, and no one lives there.

es.L: Contra él han rugido leoncillos, \q han dado su voz; \q han hecho de su tierra una desolación; \q sus ciudades están quemadas, sin habitante.
es.B: Leones jóvenes han rugido contra él; \q han alzado su voz. \q Han convertido su tierra en una ruina; \q sus ciudades están quemadas, y nadie vive en ellas.
es.R: Sus enemigos han rugido contra él como leones jóvenes. \q Han convertido su tierra en un desierto. \q Sus ciudades han sido quemadas, y nadie vive en ellas.

fr.L: Contre lui ont rugi des lionceaux, \q ils ont fait entendre leur voix ; \q ils ont fait de son pays une désolation ; \q ses villes sont incendiées, sans habitant.
fr.B: Des jeunes lions ont rugi contre lui ; \q ils ont donné de la voix. \q Ils ont fait de son pays une ruine ; \q ses villes sont incendiées, personne n’y habite plus.
fr.R: Des ennemis ont rugi contre lui comme de jeunes lions. \q Ils ont fait de son pays un désert. \q Ses villes ont été brûlées, et personne n’y habite plus.

sw.L: Simba wachanga wamemngurumia, \q wametoa sauti yao; \q wameifanya nchi yake kuwa ukiwa; \q miji yake imeteketezwa, haina mkaaji.
sw.B: Simba wachanga wamemngurumia; \q wamepaza sauti zao. \q Wameifanya nchi yake kuwa magofu; \q miji yake imeteketezwa, hakuna anayeishi humo.
sw.R: Maadui wamemngurumia kama simba wachanga. \q Wameifanya nchi yake kuwa jangwa. \q Miji yake imeteketezwa kwa moto, na hakuna mtu anayeishi humo.

decisions.choice: young lions: invading armies
decisions.reason: The prophets picture the nations that attack Israel as lions (4:7; 5:6; Isaiah 5:29). In Jeremiah's lifetime the northern kingdom had long since been laid waste by Assyria, and Judah too had lost towns (Isaiah 1:7).

decisions.choice: are burned: the reading tradition's plural
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has a singular verb and the reading tradition a plural; both mean that the cities are burned. Some take the verb from a related word, "laid waste"; the sense is little changed.

decisions.choice: enemies ... like young lions
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemies the lions stand for (m1) and folds the two lines about their roaring into one.

source.text: גַּם־בְּנֵי־נֹ֖ף וְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס יִרְע֖וּךְ קָדְקֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Also [the] sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes graze you [on the] crown of [the] head.

en.L: Even the sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes \q graze on the crown of your head.
en.B: Even the people of Memphis and Tahpanhes \q are stripping the crown of your head bare.
en.R: Even the Egyptians from Memphis and Tahpanhes \q are leaving your head stripped bare.

es.L: Aun los hijos de Menfis y de Tafnes \q te pacen la coronilla de la cabeza.
es.B: Aun la gente de Menfis y de Tafnes \q te está dejando pelada la coronilla.
es.R: Aun los egipcios de Menfis y de Tafnes \q te están dejando la cabeza rapada.

fr.L: Même les fils de Memphis et de Tahpanhès \q te tondent le sommet de la tête.
fr.B: Même les gens de Memphis et de Tahpanhès \q te rasent le sommet du crâne.
fr.R: Même les Égyptiens de Memphis et de Tahpanhès \q te laissent la tête rasée.

sw.L: Hata wana wa Memfisi na Tahpanhesi \q wamekunyoa utosi wa kichwa chako.
sw.B: Hata watu wa Memfisi na Tahpanhesi \q wanakinyoa kichwa chako hadi kubaki kipara.
sw.R: Hata Wamisri wa Memfisi na Tahpanhesi \q wanakiacha kichwa chako kikiwa wazi.

decisions.choice: graze: strip bare as cattle strip a field
alternatives: have broken the crown of your head
have shaved the crown of your head
decisions.reason: As the text is written, the verb is "graze" or "feed on": Egypt has cropped the crown of Israel's head bare, a picture of shame and loss. The same consonants can also be read as "break" or "crush" ("have broken the crown of your head"), and some have suggested "shave", a sign of disgrace. The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Memphis and Tahpanhes: cities of Egypt
decisions.reason: Memphis (in Hebrew *Noph*) was the old capital of Lower Egypt, and Tahpanhes a border fortress in the eastern delta, where Jeremiah was later taken (43:7-9). Judah looked to Egypt for help, but Egypt too brought it harm. In Jeremiah's youth Pharaoh Neco killed King Josiah and put Judah under tribute (2 Kings 23:29-35). The written text and the reading tradition spell Tahpanhes slightly differently.

decisions.choice: sons (Literal); people (Balanced); the Egyptians (Readable); graze / stripping bare / leaving stripped bare
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a city means its people. Balanced and Readable give the sense of the grazing picture (m1); Readable names the people as Egyptians.

decisions.choice: "Menfis", "Tafnes"; "te pacen" (L); "te está dejando pelada" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Egyptian cities in their usual Spanish forms ("Tafnes", as the terms note gives it). Literal keeps the picture of cattle grazing; Balanced and Readable say it means stripping bare, as the English does. From here Israel is addressed as a woman, "tú".

decisions.choice: Memfisi, Tahpanhesi
decisions.reason: The English names the city Memphis at every level; Swahili gives its usual name "Memfisi" rather than a transliteration of the Hebrew Noph, and Tahpanhes in the form the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: wamekunyoa (Literal); wanakinyoa ... kipara (Balanced); wanakiacha ... wazi (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Graze" is pictured as shaving the head bare, a mark of shame in Swahili too; the grazing image does not carry over on the head.

decisions.choice: "Memphis", "Tahpanhès"; "te tondent" (L); "te rasent" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Memphis is the usual French name of the city the Hebrew calls Noph; "tondre" keeps the picture of stripping bare (m1) in a verb French uses of a head, where "brouter" would not be understood.

source.text: הֲלוֹא־זֹ֖את תַּעֲשֶׂה־לָּ֑ךְ עָזְבֵךְ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִךְ בְּעֵ֖ת מוֹלִיכֵ֥ךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] not this [that] you do to yourself, [by] your forsaking Yahweh your God at [the] time [he was] leading you in the way?

en.L: Have you not done this to yourself \q by forsaking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God \q at the time when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was leading you in the way?
en.B: Is this not what you have done to yourself \q in forsaking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God \q while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was leading you on the way?
en.R: You have brought this trouble on yourself! \q You turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God \q while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was leading you on the right road.

es.L: ¿No te has hecho esto a ti misma \q al abandonar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q en el tiempo en que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te guiaba por el camino?
es.B: ¿No es esto lo que te has hecho a ti misma \q al abandonar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te guiaba por el camino?
es.R: ¡Tú misma te has buscado este problema! \q Le diste la espalda {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te guiaba por el buen camino.

fr.L: N’est-ce pas cela que tu t’es fait à toi-même, \q en abandonnant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu \q au temps où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te conduisait dans le chemin ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas toi qui t’es attiré cela, \q en abandonnant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu \q alors qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te guidait sur la route ?
fr.R: C’est toi-même qui as causé ce malheur ! \q Tu t’es détournée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu \q alors qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te conduisait sur le bon chemin.

sw.L: Je, hukujitendea haya wewe mwenyewe \q kwa kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako \q wakati alipokuwa akikuongoza njiani?
sw.B: Je, hili si jambo ulilojitendea wewe mwenyewe \q kwa kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako \q wakati {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alipokuwa akikuongoza njiani?
sw.R: Wewe mwenyewe umejiletea taabu hii! \q Ulimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako \q wakati {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alipokuwa akikuongoza katika njia iliyo sawa.

decisions.choice: Have you not done this to yourself?: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question answers verse 14. Israel's ruin is not bad luck or God's failure; it is the result of leaving the God who was guiding it (verse 19).

decisions.choice: leading you in the way: God guiding his people as on a journey
decisions.reason: The words recall God leading Israel through the wilderness (verse 6; Deuteronomy 1:31-33; 8:2) and point to his guidance in the way of life he taught. They left him in the middle of the journey.

decisions.choice: You have brought this trouble on yourself! ... the right road
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies (m1) and adds "right" to show what "the way" means here.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה מַה־לָּךְ֙ לְדֶ֣רֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת מֵ֣י שִׁח֑וֹר וּמַה־לָּךְ֙ לְדֶ֣רֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת מֵ֥י נָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And now what [is it] to you to [the] way of Egypt, to drink [the] waters of Shihor? And what [is it] to you to [the] way of Assyria, to drink [the] waters of [the] River?

en.L: And now, what [is it] to you [to go] on the road to Egypt, \q to drink the waters of Shihor? \q And what [is it] to you [to go] on the road to Assyria, \q to drink the waters of the River?
en.B: So now, what do you gain by taking the road to Egypt \q to drink the waters of the Shihor? \q What do you gain by taking the road to Assyria \q to drink the waters of the Euphrates?
en.R: So why go down the road to Egypt \q to drink water from the Nile? \q Why go off on the road to Assyria \q to drink water from the Euphrates River?

es.L: Y ahora, ¿qué [tienes] tú con el camino a Egipto, \q para beber las aguas del Sihor? \q ¿Y qué [tienes] tú con el camino a Asiria, \q para beber las aguas del Río?
es.B: Y ahora, ¿qué ganas con tomar el camino a Egipto \q para beber las aguas del Sihor? \q ¿Qué ganas con tomar el camino a Asiria \q para beber las aguas del Éufrates?
es.R: Entonces, ¿para qué bajas por el camino a Egipto \q a beber agua del Nilo? \q ¿Para qué te vas por el camino a Asiria \q a beber agua del río Éufrates?

fr.L: Et maintenant, qu’as-tu [à faire] sur le chemin de l’Égypte, \q pour boire les eaux du Shihor ? \q Et qu’as-tu [à faire] sur le chemin de l’Assyrie, \q pour boire les eaux du Fleuve ?
fr.B: Et maintenant, que gagnes-tu à prendre le chemin de l’Égypte \q pour boire les eaux du Shihor ? \q Que gagnes-tu à prendre le chemin de l’Assyrie \q pour boire les eaux de l’Euphrate ?
fr.R: Alors pourquoi prendre la route de l’Égypte \q pour boire l’eau du Nil ? \q Pourquoi partir sur la route de l’Assyrie \q pour boire l’eau du fleuve Euphrate ?

sw.L: Na sasa, una nini wewe na njia ya Misri, \q kunywa maji ya Shihori? \q Na una nini wewe na njia ya Ashuru, \q kunywa maji ya Mto?
sw.B: Basi sasa, utapata faida gani kwa kuishika njia ya Misri \q ili kunywa maji ya Shihori? \q Utapata faida gani kwa kuishika njia ya Ashuru \q ili kunywa maji ya mto Frati?
sw.R: Basi kwa nini kwenda katika njia ya Misri \q kunywa maji ya mto Naili? \q Kwa nini kwenda katika njia ya Ashuru \q kunywa maji ya mto Frati?

decisions.choice: Shihor and the River: the Nile and the Euphrates
decisions.reason: Shihor was a branch or channel of the Nile on Egypt's eastern edge (Joshua 13:3; Isaiah 23:3), and "the River" is the Euphrates, the river of Mesopotamia (Genesis 31:21). Each river stands for the great power that lived by it.

decisions.choice: to drink the waters: to seek help from Egypt and Assyria
decisions.reason: Judah's kings looked to Egypt and to Assyria by turns for protection and paid them for it (2 Kings 16:7-8; 17:4; Hosea 7:11). The picture of drinking points back to verse 13: they left the spring of living water to drink from foreign rivers.

decisions.choice: what is it to you?: what business do you have, what good will it do
decisions.reason: The question asks what reason they have to go, and what they hope to gain. It expects the answer: none.

decisions.choice: Shihor (Literal), the Shihor (Balanced), the Nile (Readable); the River (Literal), the Euphrates (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for "the River", as in Isaiah. Readable names the Shihor by its river, the Nile (m1).

decisions.choice: "el Sihor" (L, B), "el Nilo" (R); "el Río" (L), "el Éufrates" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English levels: Literal keeps the Hebrew names, Balanced names the Euphrates, Readable names both rivers.

decisions.choice: Shihori (Literal, Balanced), mto Naili (Readable); Mto (Literal), mto Frati (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The rivers named as the English levels name them; "Shihori" as Joshua 13:3 and "mto Frati" as 1 Kings 14:15.

decisions.choice: "le Shihor" (L, B), "le Nil" (R); "le Fleuve" (L), "l’Euphrate" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for "the River" in the prophets: Literal keeps the title, capitalised as a name, and Balanced and Readable name it, as the English does.

source.text: תְּיַסְּרֵ֣ךְ רָעָתֵ֗ךְ וּמְשֻֽׁבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ תּוֹכִחֻ֔ךְ וּדְעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ כִּי־רַ֣ע וָמָ֔ר עָזְבֵ֖ךְ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יִךְ וְלֹ֤א פַחְדָּתִי֙ אֵלַ֔יִךְ נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Will discipline you your evil, and your turnings away will rebuke you; and know and see that evil and bitter [is] your forsaking Yahweh your God, and not [is] dread of me toward you, declares [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: Your evil will discipline you, and your turnings away will rebuke you. \q Know and see that it is evil and bitter \q for you to forsake {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q and that the dread of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not in you, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: Your own wickedness will punish you, and your turning away will convict you. \q Know, then, and see what an evil and bitter thing it is \q for you to forsake {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q with no dread of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in you, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: Your own evil will punish you. Your turning away will prove you wrong. \q Understand this and see it clearly: \q it is evil and bitter to leave {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God \q and to have no fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: Tu maldad te castigará, y tus apostasías te reprenderán. \q Sabe, pues, y mira que es malo y amargo \q que abandones {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios, \q y que no haya temor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} en ti, \q declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Tu propia maldad te castigará, y tu apostasía te acusará. \q Reconoce, pues, y mira qué cosa tan mala y amarga es \q abandonar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q y no tener temor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Tu propio mal te castigará. Tu infidelidad te dejará en evidencia. \q Entiende esto y míralo claramente: \q es malo y amargo dejar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q y no tener temor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Ta méchanceté te corrigera, et tes infidélités te réprimanderont. \q Sache et vois qu’il est mauvais et amer \q d’abandonner {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, \q et que la crainte de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} n’est pas en toi, \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Ta propre méchanceté te punira, et tes infidélités te condamneront. \q Reconnais donc et vois combien il est mauvais et amer \q d’abandonner {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, \q sans avoir aucune crainte de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Ton propre mal te punira. Ton infidélité montrera que tu as tort. \q Comprends-le et vois-le clairement : \q c’est mauvais et amer d’abandonner {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu \q et de ne pas avoir de respect pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Uovu wako utakuadhibu, na maasi yako yatakukemea. \q Basi ujue na kuona ya kuwa ni uovu na uchungu \q kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, \q na kwamba kunicha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hakumo ndani yako, \q asema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Uovu wako mwenyewe utakuadhibu, na kuniacha kwako kutakuhukumu. \q Basi jua na uone jinsi lilivyo jambo baya na chungu \q wewe kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, \q bila kuwa na hofu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ndani yako, \q asema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
